info.title: Transactional Email Service
info.description: Transactional email service with templating, deduplication, and recipient resolution

reason.description: Why the recipient was not sent to: 'duplicate' (deduplicated), 'self_action' (a staff-routed alert whose acting person, metadata.email, is this staff recipient under any of their addresses), or the delivery error

eventType.description: Event type determining which template to use and which dedup strategy applies. Once-only events (waitlist, welcome, signup_notification, first_payment): sent at most once per recipient. Daily events (user_active): sent at most once per recipient per day. Product-scoped events (webinar_welcome, j_minus_3, j_minus_2, j_minus_1, j_day): sent once per recipient per productId. Monthly per-brand events (audience_fully_contacted): sent at most once per org per brand per calendar month. Org-daily events (provider_credits_exhausted): sent at most once per org per calendar day, with no recipient in the key. Any other event type has NO dedup and will send every time. Staff notification events (signup_notification, signin_notification, user_active, brand_daily_budget_changed, payment_method_removed, staff_daily_digest, provider_credits_exhausted, campaign_failing, audience_refill_failed, trigger_silent, trigger_occurrence_stuck) are delivered to the internal staff recipient list, never to the customer.

brandIds.description: Brand IDs for tracking (one or more UUIDs)

productId.description: Product/instance ID, required for product-scoped dedup (e.g. webinar ID)

recipientEmail.description: Direct recipient email (overrides client-service resolution if provided)

bccEmails.description: Blind-copy recipient email addresses, forwarded as provider-level BCC recipients and never rendered into templates or stored in metadata. On a customer-facing event kevin@distribute.you is added to whatever is supplied here; on a staff-routed event nothing is added.

ccEmails.description: Visible-copy recipient email addresses, forwarded as provider-level Cc recipients and never rendered into templates or stored in metadata. Every recipient of the message can see them on the Cc header, and a reply-all reaches them. Nothing is ever added here: a caller that names none gets no Cc at all. Rejected on the staff-routed events that already refuse a caller-supplied recipient list.

replyToEmail.description: Reply address of the email being sent: forwarded as the provider-level Reply-To, so a recipient who hits Reply writes to this address. Never rendered into templates or stored in metadata. When absent, replies go to kevin@distribute.you exactly as before. Rejected on the staff-routed events that already refuse a caller-supplied recipient list.

htmlBody.description: The HTML a send of this event would carry, the "Revenue made easy." sign-off included where the event is a distribute.you message to a customer. email-gateway appends its signature and unsubscribe footer at send time, so those are absent here.

from.description: The template's own sender, or null for the gateway default.

eventType.description: The event whose registered template to render.

metadata.description: Template variables for {{variable}} interpolation, as a send would pass them.

eventId.description: This service's record of the send.

runId.description: The org-less platform run the send is declared under.

code.description: Machine code for the refusal or failure.

eventType.description: The template to send. Only an allowlisted event type is accepted: `agent_signup_code` (requires metadata `code`, `expiresInMinutes`). Any other name is refused with 400 `code: "event_not_orgless"`.

recipientEmail.description: The address to mail. The person behind it has no account yet.

metadata.description: Template variables for {{variable}} interpolation. The event's required keys must be present and non-empty.

sent.description: True when this call delivered the alert. False only on a duplicate.

duplicate.description: True when this event id was already delivered: nothing was sent again. Not an error.

runId.description: The org-less platform run the send is declared under. Null on a duplicate.

code.description: Machine code for the refusal or failure.

missing.description: On `missing_metadata`: the metadata keys that are missing or blank.

eventType.description: The staff alert to raise. Closed list: `sending_domain_blocklisted` (requires metadata `domain`, `listName`, `listedSince`, `listAnswer`, `mailboxesAffected`, `actionTaken`, `removalUrl`). Any other name is refused with 400 `code: "event_not_platform_staff_alert"`.

eventId.description: Caller-chosen id of ONE occurrence of the fact (e.g. `<domain>:<list>:<listedSince>`). The same id delivers once, ever: a second call answers 200 `duplicate: true`. A call whose delivery failed (502) can be retried with the same id and sends.

metadata.description: Template variables of the event type, all non-empty strings. A missing or blank key is a 400 `missing_metadata` naming it in `missing`.

domain.description: The sending domain that is listed.

listedSince.description: When the listing was first seen, ISO 8601.

listAnswer.description: What the list answered for the domain.

mailboxesAffected.description: Comma-separated mailboxes on the domain. May be long.

actionTaken.example: The 5 mailboxes no longer start new sequences.

removalUrl.description: Where to request removal from the list.

inboxPct.description: Inbox % at that provider among the mailboxes still allowed to mail it (after the automatic cut). A number, no % sign.

thresholdPct.description: The market bar, a number, no % sign.

mailboxesCut.description: How many mailboxes the automatic cut already took off that provider.

from.description: Sender address for this template, e.g. "Display Name <email@domain.com>". If omitted, the email gateway default is used.

layout.description: "brand" (the default for a new template): a customer email whose rendered htmlBody is not a full HTML document (no <!DOCTYPE html> / <html>) is delivered inside the distribute.you layout (official logo, white card, footer) and its textBody ends with the distribute.you sign-off; register only the card's content. "none": delivered exactly as registered, for a template addressed to staff rather than a customer. Omitted on an existing template: its current layout is kept. Staff-routed event types and templates sent from outside distribute.you are never wrapped, and a full HTML document is never wrapped.

stream.description: How an email from this template is delivered. "transactional": person-to-person mail the recipient is meant to answer with Reply, like a normal email from a person. It goes out on the Postmark transactional stream with no List-Unsubscribe header and no Unsubscribe footer, and it is sent exactly as registered: no distribute.you layout and no "Revenue made easy." sign-off (the recipient's reply quotes the message, so anything we add travels into their conversation). Reply-To stays as the send sets it (replyToEmail, else the founder). Never use it for anything a recipient can ask to stop receiving. "broadcast" (the default for a new template): today's delivery, broadcast stream plus the Unsubscribe footer. Omitted on an existing template: its current stream is kept. Mailing-list updates never use templates and always keep their unsubscribe.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `after` to continue. An empty page returns the cursor sent; null only when nothing was ever sent.

id.description: Stable id of this send (one per recipient). Idempotency key for a mirror.

eventType.description: The template the email was rendered from.

orgId.description: Internal org UUID the send was billed to. Null on an org-less send (a person with no account yet) and on February 2026 rows that predate internal org ids (stored as "legacy" or a Clerk org_ id).

messageSource.description: stored = the exact message put on the wire. replayed = a send made before messages were stored (2026-10-24), re-rendered from its current template with the stored variables: close to, not guaranteed byte-equal. unavailable = such a send whose template no longer exists (subject and bodies null).

status.description: valid = the id names a subscriber still on the list. revoked = it was given to a subscriber since removed from the list (names nobody). unknown = well-formed but never given. tampered = not an id this service minted (wrong length, alphabet or checksum).

name.description: Always null today: a list stores bare addresses.

subscriber.description: Present only when status is valid.

list.description: Present only when status is valid.

subjects.description: Distinct subscriber addresses named (one subscriber per address).

checks.description: Past checks of those addresses a release asked for: one email_checked each.

subjectsWithoutCheck.description: Addresses no release check holds (never verified, or only invalid / undecided).

parked.description: Checks apollo-service parked for declaration by this call (0 on a dry run, 0 on a replay).

dryRun.description: true = apollo-service only counts; nothing is parked.

resolved.description: Subscribers whose address is a lead-service lead: one equivalence each.

notALead.description: Subscribers whose address is nobody's lead (yet): stated on a later pass once they are.

ambiguous.description: Subscribers whose address two leads hold: never a pick, nothing stated.

recorded.description: Equivalences newly recorded by runs-service (0 on a dry run).

refused.description: Items runs-service refused (one target per subject, one hop, immutable), with its reason. The rest of their call is still stated.

dryRun.description: true = resolve and count; nothing is stated at runs-service.

releaseRuns.description: Release runs holding at least one past send.

occurrences.description: Past `message_sent` occurrences our rows hold (one per release run x subscriber reached).

calls.description: runs-service batch calls (one per release run x UTC day, <= 1000 occurrences each).

recorded.description: Occurrences newly recorded by runs-service (0 on a dry run, 0 on a replay).

dryRun.description: true = count what would be declared and write nothing.

optedOut.description: True when Postmark is suppressing sends to this address — the member used the native unsubscribe, complained, or hard-bounced. Read from the Postmark broadcast stream's suppression list, per address, and reused for up to a minute; this service stores no opt-out flag of its own. A send re-checks every recipient against Postmark and never reuses that answer.

optedOutReason.description: Postmark's own reason: "ManualSuppression" (unsubscribed), "SpamComplaint" or "HardBounce". Null when not suppressed.

added.description: Addresses newly added to the list

skipped.description: Addresses already on the list, or repeated inside the blob

rejected.description: Fragments that could not be read as an email address

raw.description: A pasted blob of email addresses. Comma-, semicolon-, tab- or newline-separated; `Name <email@example.com>` pairs are accepted. Duplicates and existing members are skipped, so re-pasting the same blob is a no-op.

htmlBody.description: The HTML a recipient would receive for this body, byte-for-byte what a send of the same body produces. email-gateway appends the unsubscribe footer at send time, so it is absent here. For an authored `htmlBody` this is that document unchanged.

textBody.description: The plain-text part: the markdown itself for a markdown body, and for an authored one the supplied `textBody` or the text derived from the HTML.

bodyKind.description: Which body this preview rendered: "markdown" was rendered by this service, "html" was returned as authored.

unrenderableImages.description: Image URLs no mail client renders. A send of this body would be refused with a 400 naming these; empty means the body is sendable.

body.description: The update body as markdown, exactly as it would be sent. Rendered by the same code a real send uses. Mutually exclusive with `htmlBody`; exactly one of the two is required.

htmlBody.description: A document staff authored, previewed exactly as a send treats it: returned unchanged. Mutually exclusive with `body`.

textBody.description: The plain-text part for an `htmlBody` preview. Omit it and the derived one comes back, which is what a send with no `textBody` would use. Only valid beside `htmlBody`.

status.description: "sent" — every recipient succeeded. "partial" — some did. "failed" — none did, which is answered with a 502 carrying the provider's reason.

from.description: The address the update went out from

skippedOptedOut.description: Members not mailed because the provider is suppressing them

failures.description: Recipients whose send failed, with the provider's reason

error.description: The provider's own reason for refusing, verbatim — an unverified sender signature, say

body.description: The update body, authored as markdown — headings, bold, links, tables, and `![alt](https://…)` inline images. Rendered to HTML with all styling inlined on the elements (mail clients strip `<style>` and `<head>`); the markdown itself is sent as the plain-text part. SVG images are rejected with a 400 — Gmail, Outlook and Yahoo show the alt text instead of the image, so use PNG or JPEG. A discreet unsubscribe is appended downstream by email-gateway; do not add one here. Mutually exclusive with `htmlBody`; exactly one of the two is required.

htmlBody.description: A complete HTML document staff authored, sent to every recipient byte-for-byte as supplied: nothing is re-rendered, no styles are inlined for you, and it is not wrapped in the markdown template's shell. Use it for a designed newsletter — table layout, inline styles on every element, hosted PNG or JPEG images, a 600px measure — which markdown cannot express. Everything else applies unchanged: email-gateway appends the unsubscribe footer, suppressed members are skipped, one message goes per recipient, and `from` selects the sender. SVG images are still refused with a 400, since they arrive as broken placeholders whoever authored the markup. Mutually exclusive with `body`; exactly one of the two is required.

textBody.description: The plain-text part for an `htmlBody` send. Omit it and one is derived from the HTML — tags dropped, links kept as `label (url)` — so the message always carries a text alternative. Supply it to write better prose than a derivation gives. Only valid beside `htmlBody`: a markdown update's text part is its markdown.

from.description: The address this update goes out from, for this send only. Omit it and the update leaves the investor-update sender, kevin@distribute.you, exactly as every update did before this field existed. State one to send from another identity — a newsletter leaving a dedicated subdomain, say. The address must be a sender Postmark has verified: an unverified one is refused by the provider and the whole send fails with its reason, never silently falling back to the default.

body.description: Markdown as authored, and null when the update was authored as HTML — there was no markdown

bodyKind.description: How this update was authored: "markdown" was rendered by this service, "html" was sent as the author wrote it.

from.description: The address this update went out from

created.description: False when this request restated an update already being released to this list, in which case the release the first request created is returned untouched and nothing new was started.

estimatedDays.description: recipientCount divided by dailyLimit, rounded up

status.description: "running" — the worker is releasing it. "paused" — staff stopped it and may resume. "cancelled" — staff ended it; it never resumes. "halted" — it stopped itself because the provider's delivery outcomes for it went bad, and staff were told. "completed" — every address is accounted for.

haltedReason.description: Why a halted release stopped, in the words the staff alert repeated. Null otherwise.

recipientCount.description: Addresses the list held when the release was created

reached.description: Addresses a message has gone out to

failed.description: Addresses whose send failed, or whose claim outlived the worker holding it

skippedOptedOut.description: Addresses the provider was suppressing at the moment their slice was sent — checked per slice, so somebody who unsubscribes on day one is skipped on day five

skippedUndeliverable.description: Addresses verified (apollo-service BounceVerify) just before their slice was sent and NOT sent because the verdict was anything but `valid` (catch_all, unknown, risky, invalid). The verdict is stored per recipient. They do not consume the daily allowance.

inFlight.description: Addresses a worker is holding right now

todayAllowance.description: Messages this release may send today: its daily limit

todayUsed.description: How much of today's allowance is spent, in-flight addresses included

estimatedDaysRemaining.description: How many more UTC days the addresses still waiting need at the release's current pace, today included when today can still carry somebody. 0 when nobody is waiting, and 0 for a release that is not going to run again. It is arithmetic over the pace and the ledger: it says nothing about the provider's outcomes.

nextSliceSize.description: How many the next tick would take, which is 0 when today's allowance is spent or the release is not running

body.description: The update body, authored as markdown, rendered here exactly as the synchronous send renders it. Mutually exclusive with `htmlBody`; exactly one of the two is required.

htmlBody.description: A complete HTML document staff authored, sent to every recipient byte-for-byte as supplied. Mutually exclusive with `body`; exactly one of the two is required.

textBody.description: The plain-text part for an `htmlBody` release. Omit it and one is derived from the HTML. Only valid beside `htmlBody`.

from.description: The address this release goes out from. Omit it and it leaves kevin@distribute.you, the same default the synchronous send takes. It must be a sender Postmark has verified: an unverified one is refused by the provider, and every message in the release fails with its reason rather than falling back to anything.

dailyLimit.description: The most messages this release may send per UTC calendar day. Required, with no default: the pace is the reason a release exists and this service will not pick one on staff's behalf. The day's allowance is spread across the day rather than spent at midnight, and a day where the allowance is reached simply stops until the next one. The ceiling is 28800, which is the most the worker's own pace can deliver in a day; a larger number is refused rather than silently under-delivered. Pick it for the sending reputation you have, not the list you hold: a subdomain two weeks old with a few hundred messages of lifetime volume is throttled or foldered by Gmail and Outlook if it jumps to tens of thousands.

The new most-messages-per-UTC-day for this release, governing from the moment it is accepted. Raising it makes more of today's allowance available at once, without waiting for tomorrow. Lowering it below what today has already sent claws nothing back and fails nothing: the day simply rests and the new pace governs from the next one. The ceiling is 28800, the same one the create route applies, for the same reason.

verificationUnavailable.description: Slices whose verdicts could not be obtained; nothing in them was sent and they return to pending.

skippedBusy.description: True when another tick was already running and this call did nothing

post.description:
Send a templated lifecycle email. Resolves recipients via user ID (client-service) or direct email. One of userId (from x-user-id header) or recipientEmail is required.

**Required headers:** `x-org-id`, `x-user-id`, `x-run-id`

**Deduplication:** The dedup strategy depends on eventType:
- **Once-only** (waitlist, welcome, signup_notification, first_payment): sent at most once per recipient, ever. Dedup key: `{orgId}:{eventType}:{userId or recipientEmail}`.
- **Daily** (user_active): sent at most once per recipient per day. Dedup key: `{orgId}:{eventType}:{identifier}:{YYYY-MM-DD}`.
- **Product-scoped** (webinar_welcome, j_minus_3, j_minus_2, j_minus_1, j_day): sent once per recipient per productId. Dedup key: `{orgId}:{eventType}:{recipientEmail}:{productId}`.
- **Monthly per-brand** (audience_fully_contacted): sent at most once per org per brand per calendar month. Brand + month derive from the existing request (x-brand-id header / brandIds body). Dedup key: `{orgId}:{eventType}:{sortedBrandIds}:{YYYY-MM}`.
- **Org-daily** (provider_credits_exhausted): sent at most once per org per calendar day. No recipient and no user in the key, so a machine caller deduplicates exactly like one with an acting user. Dedup key: `{orgId}:{eventType}:{YYYY-MM-DD}`.
- **Campaign-daily** (campaign_failing): sent at most once per campaign per calendar day. Dedup key: `{orgId}:campaign_failing:{metadata.campaignId}:{YYYY-MM-DD}`. Requires non-empty `metadata.campaignId`, `consecutiveFailures`, `failingSince`, `retryInterval`; accepts no `recipientEmail`, `bccEmails`, `ccEmails` or `replyToEmail`.
- **Campaign-daily** (audience_refill_failed): same bound, own key `{orgId}:audience_refill_failed:{metadata.campaignId}:{YYYY-MM-DD}`. Requires non-empty `metadata.campaignId`, `brandId`, `refillOutcome`; optional `campaignName`, `brandName`, `refillDetail`, `whereToLook`; accepts no `recipientEmail`, `bccEmails`, `ccEmails` or `replyToEmail`.
- **Trigger-daily, fleet-wide** (trigger_silent): sent at most once per trigger per calendar day, whatever the org. Dedup key: `trigger_silent:{metadata.triggerId}:{YYYY-MM-DD}` (no org: the trigger list is the same for every customer). Requires non-empty `metadata.triggerId`, `triggerLabel`, `silentSince`, `silentDays`, `liveCampaignCount`; optional `firedBy`, `whereToLook`; accepts no `recipientEmail`, `bccEmails`, `ccEmails` or `replyToEmail`. `x-user-id` is billing context only: never resolved into an actor, never suppressed as the recipient's own action.
- **Once per occurrence, fleet-wide** (trigger_occurrence_stuck): sent at most once per trigger occurrence, ever. Dedup key: `trigger_occurrence_stuck:{metadata.occurrenceId}`. Requires non-empty `metadata.occurrenceId`, `triggerId`, `campaignId`, `brandId`, `waitingSince`, `attempts`, `lastError`; optional `campaignName`, `triggerLabel`, `prospect`, `whereToLook`; accepts no `recipientEmail`, `bccEmails`, `ccEmails` or `replyToEmail`. `x-user-id` is billing context only, never an actor.
- **No dedup** (all other event types, including brand_daily_budget_changed, payment_method_removed, staff_daily_digest and unpaid_debt_uncollectable): sends every time with no dedup.

**Staff routing:** `signup_notification`, `signin_notification`, `user_active`, `brand_daily_budget_changed`, `payment_method_removed`, `staff_daily_digest`, `provider_credits_exhausted`, `campaign_failing` (campaign-service: a campaign has failed every run for a sustained stretch), `audience_refill_failed` (campaign-service: a campaign ran out of people and the automatic audience refill gave it nobody new), `trigger_silent` (campaign-service: a reactive trigger has produced no event for days while live campaigns depend on it), `trigger_occurrence_stuck` (campaign-service: one trigger occurrence carrying a person or an item has waited undelivered because a campaign behind it cannot run) and `unpaid_debt_uncollectable` (billing-service: an org owes money and has no card to collect it on) are delivered to the internal staff recipient list instead of the customer resolved from `x-user-id`. Their metadata is enriched with the acting user's email under `email` when not already supplied — a caller with no acting user sends no actor metadata at all.

**No self-alerts:** a staff-routed event is not delivered to a staff recipient who is the acting person (`metadata.email`, caller-supplied or enriched, compared trimmed and case-insensitively against the recipient address and every other address that same person acts under, e.g. an action by kevin@distribute.you skips kevin.lourd@gmail.com): they already know what they did. That recipient comes back as `{ sent: false, reason: 'self_action' }` with a 200, and nothing is sent, recorded or tracked for it. An event with no acting person (a machine caller) is delivered as before.

**`provider_credits_exhausted`** reports that a paid third-party provider has run out of credits, so work depending on it now produces nothing. `metadata.provider` (which provider) and `metadata.reason` (why we concluded it is dry) are required and must be non-empty; `metadata.detail` carries any raw upstream status or response body and is optional. `metadata.orgId` is filled in from `x-org-id` and needs no supplying. It accepts no `recipientEmail`, no `bccEmails`, no `ccEmails` and no `replyToEmail` on any route, so it cannot reach a customer address.

`bccEmails` are delivered as provider-level BCC recipients on the primary email, and `ccEmails` as provider-level Cc recipients. Neither is rendered into templates and neither affects primary-recipient deduplication.

**Visible copy:** `ccEmails` puts an address on the Cc header, where every recipient of the message can see it and a reply-all reaches it — the right instrument when somebody is a party to the conversation rather than an observer of it. Nothing is ever added to this list: a caller that names none gets a message with no Cc at all, byte for byte as before. It is refused on the same staff-routed events that refuse `recipientEmail` and `bccEmails`.

**Blind copy and replies:** a customer-facing send is blind-copied to kevin@distribute.you, so the company sees what it tells a customer as it tells them. A caller's own `bccEmails` are kept and that one address is added to them, never in place of them. A staff-routed event carries no such blind copy — the same person is already a primary recipient on the staff list, and a second copy would deliver the message twice. Every send, staff or customer, invites replies to kevin@distribute.you so a customer who hits reply reaches a human, unless the caller names its own `replyToEmail`, in which case the Reply-To is that address instead (e.g. a forwarded prospect reply, where the customer should answer the prospect directly). `replyToEmail` is refused on the same staff-routed events that refuse `recipientEmail`, `bccEmails` and `ccEmails`.

Duplicate sends return `{ sent: false, reason: 'duplicate' }`; a staff self-alert returns `{ sent: false, reason: 'self_action' }`. To add a new event type to dedup, add it to the corresponding set in send.ts.

post.summary: Render an event's email exactly as a send would, without sending
post.description:
Resolves the event's registered template, interpolates `metadata`, and returns the message a `POST /send` of the same event would put on the wire. Nothing is sent, recorded or resolved.

Every customer-facing distribute.you email is signed with the company's why, "Revenue made easy.", as a quiet last line in both parts; it is not added to staff-routed alerts, to a template whose sender is outside distribute.you, or to a body that already carries the sentence. This preview shows exactly that.

post.summary: Send a staff-bound notification without an acting user
post.description:
For machine callers that hold an organisation and an API key but no end-user identity — e.g. stripe-service reacting to a Stripe webhook, where the customer acted inside Stripe's billing portal and no user of ours took any action.

**Required headers:** `x-org-id`. `x-user-id` and `x-run-id` are honoured when present but never required, and are never substituted with a placeholder when absent.

**Accepted event types:** staff-bound events only (`signup_notification`, `signin_notification`, `user_active`, `brand_daily_budget_changed`, `payment_method_removed`, `staff_daily_digest`, `provider_credits_exhausted`, `unpaid_debt_uncollectable`, `campaign_failing`, `audience_refill_failed`, `trigger_silent`, `trigger_occurrence_stuck`). Any other event type is rejected with 400, so no request on this path can reach a customer.

`recipientEmail`, `bccEmails`, `ccEmails` and `replyToEmail` are rejected with 400: delivery is to the internal staff recipient list only.

**`provider_credits_exhausted`** — the event type a backend service raises when it detects that a paid third-party provider has run out of credits (e.g. apollo-service on Apollo.io credit exhaustion). Send it here: an org and an API key are enough, no acting user is needed.

```json
{
  "eventType": "provider_credits_exhausted",
  "metadata": {
    "provider": "Apollo.io",
    "reason": "people/search returned 402 with credits_remaining: 0 on 3 consecutive calls",
    "detail": "HTTP 402 {\"error\":\"insufficient_credits\",\"credits_remaining\":0}"
  }
}
```

`metadata.provider` and `metadata.reason` are required and must be non-empty, else 400 — a staff alert with blanks where the facts belong is not actionable. `metadata.detail` is optional free-form room for the raw upstream status or response body. `metadata.orgId` is filled in from `x-org-id`. It is deduped once per org per calendar day (key `{orgId}:provider_credits_exhausted:{YYYY-MM-DD}`), so a service hitting the credit wall on thousands of consecutive operations mails staff once; the repeats return `{ sent: false, reason: "duplicate" }` like any other deduplicated send, and the next calendar day the alert can raise again. Its template is registered by this service on boot, not by the caller.

Dedup, template resolution, run tracking, the no-self-alert rule (a staff recipient who is the acting person in `metadata.email`, under any of their addresses, gets `{ sent: false, reason: 'self_action' }`, nothing sent) and response shape are identical to `POST /send`. `payment_method_removed` and `staff_daily_digest` belong to no dedup set, so every occurrence sends. The `staff_daily_digest` template is owned and registered by the customer dashboard under that exact name.

parameters.name: x-org-id
parameters.description: Internal org UUID from client-service

parameters.name: x-user-id
parameters.description: Internal user UUID from client-service. Optional on this route — omit it when there is no acting user.

post.summary: Send an allowlisted template to a person who has no account yet, platform-paid
post.description:
For a backend caller that must mail somebody BEFORE any organisation or user exists: client-service's one-time sign-up code for an AI agent opening an account against an email. The send names no organisation and no user at any hop, and the platform pays for it: it is declared on an org-less platform run in runs-service and relayed to email-gateway `POST /platform/send` (org-less, platform-paid, Postmark transactional stream: no unsubscribe footer), so no customer org is authorized, created or charged.

**Headers:** `X-API-Key` only. `x-org-id` and `x-user-id` are refused with 400 `org_identity_not_accepted`: this path is org-less by definition, and a send that has an org belongs on `POST /send`.

**Accepted event types (closed list):** `agent_signup_code` (requires metadata `code`, `expiresInMinutes`). Any other name: 400 `event_not_orgless`. A missing or blank required metadata key: 400 `missing_metadata`. An allowlisted name whose template is not registered: 404 `template_not_found`. The template is the caller's own (`PUT /platform-templates`), delivered exactly as registered when its stream is `transactional`.

**Not deduplicated:** every call sends; asking for a new code twice delivers twice.

**No copy:** no Cc, no Bcc (the founder blind copy every other customer-facing send carries is NOT added: a one-time code reaches only the person it is for), and no caller-chosen Reply-To (the founder default applies). The body is strict: any other field is a 400.

**Failure is loud:** 200 means the provider accepted the message. A run that could not be opened is 502 `run_failed`; a delivery the gateway refused or failed is 502 `delivery_failed`, with the upstream status in `error`. Nothing on this path ever returns 2xx without a send.

post.summary: Release a written update to a mailing list over several days
post.description: Staff-only. A release sends one written update to a mailing list over several days at a stated daily pace. Nothing is sent inside the request that creates it: an in-process worker releases it afterwards, so no caller holds a connection open and a restart changes nothing. Every address is a ledger row from the moment the release is created, which is what makes never mailing anybody twice structural rather than careful, and what progress is counted from. Provider suppression is re-read for each slice at the moment that slice is sent. The body is stated exactly as the synchronous send takes it — `body` as markdown or `htmlBody` as a document staff authored — plus `dailyLimit`, which has no default. The answer comes back in about a second whatever the list's size and reports how many recipients the release covers and the pace it will follow. Restating an update already being released to this list returns that release with `created: false` rather than starting a second one over the same people.

patch.summary: Change how fast a release goes out, while it is going out
patch.description: Staff-only. A release sends one written update to a mailing list over several days at a stated daily pace. Nothing is sent inside the request that creates it: an in-process worker releases it afterwards, so no caller holds a connection open and a restart changes nothing. Every address is a ledger row from the moment the release is created, which is what makes never mailing anybody twice structural rather than careful, and what progress is counted from. Provider suppression is re-read for each slice at the moment that slice is sent. The pace a release was created with is a guess made before the first message went out; this changes it on the evidence the release has since produced.
